selected_problem: Fresh-main reality testing found that a timed-out one-shot validation killed only its shell process. Background descendants survived, inherited the shell pipes, delayed the timeout result for about ten seconds, and performed a late filesystem write after the validator had already declared a timeout.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: The committed four-mode router selects DEEP_DEVELOPMENT through the singular evidence-rich bottleneck gate; no mode rotation was forced.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC or RCL success receipt is claimed. Selection/routing use committed DWAC source-contract replay over fresh canonical main while the provider remained transiently unavailable.

pre_fix_reproduction.command: node child-write-after-600ms in background; sleep 10; runCommand timeout=120ms
pre_fix_reproduction.observed: timedOut=true but runCommand returned after about 10012ms and /tmp/twc-late-sentinel existed with content late after the timeout.

changes: runCommand adds opt-in containProcessTree=false, preserving existing callers by default.
On POSIX, contained one-shot commands run in their own detached process group.
Timeout sends SIGTERM to the whole process group and schedules a bounded SIGKILL fallback after 750ms.
runAcceptance opts into process-tree containment together with its existing minimal environment and isolated shell controls.
Persistent interactive terminal semantics are unchanged.
A focused POSIX regression proves timeout returns promptly and a delayed descendant can no longer write its sentinel file.

validation.tests: 10/10 PASS; 0 skipped on the POSIX validation host

truth_boundaries: POSIX process-group containment is reality-verified; equivalent Windows descendant-tree containment is not claimed by this change and remains a residual gap.
This is not an OS-level filesystem/network sandbox; validation commands can still access resources permitted to the Taowind Code process while they are running.
Arbitrary complex repository semantic synthesis remains UNRESOLVED.
Filesystem crash-level atomicity for arbitrary I/O/process failure remains unresolved.
No GitHub Actions were intentionally triggered or rerun, no force push was used, and no credential, payment, formal Release or destructive/irreversible external action was performed.
